title: Inductive-inductive types from inductive types without UIP
formal: In the intensional Martin-Löf type theory \(\mathsf T\) specified below, can every finitary inductive-inductive signature be implemented using the existing type formers, with its full dependent eliminator and propositional constructor computation equations? More precisely, is there a uniform effective derived-rule construction which, for every finite well-formed signature \(S\), every well-formed external parameter context and every permitted universe instance, produces the sorts and constructors of an \(S\)-algebra \(A_S\) and, for every displayed \(S\)-algebra \(D\) over \(A_S\), a section of \(D\) with a proof of each constructor equation? All these terms and proofs must be derivable in \(\mathsf T\). This is the user-selected intensional specialization, approved on 16 September 2026, of the source's broader question about a UIP-free setting; it does not ask to settle every possible UIP-free foundation.
why: Inductive-inductive definitions express dependent syntax directly, including contexts and the types valid in each context. A generic reduction would identify which primitives a proof assistant needs to support such syntax while retaining identity types with higher structure. The issue concerns expressive power and dependent elimination, not merely implementation convenience: an encoding can supply all the apparent constructors yet lose the induction principle needed to use the data.
status_note: Source Remark 47 (published 2020) retains the broader UIP-free problem. On 16 September 2026 the user explicitly selected the intensional MLTT variant stated here. Checked Hugunin 2019, the December 2025 workshop programme and the May 2026 artifact; no inspected result establishes the generic construction in this base with full elimination. importance.reason: A foundational expressiveness question connecting generic dependent datatype support, representations of typed syntax and the treatment of equality in intensional and homotopical foundations.

sentences: Inductive-inductive types define mutually dependent sorts, such as contexts together with the types valid in each context.
The selected question asks whether every finitary signature can be implemented uniformly in intensional MLTT using indexed W-types and function extensionality, without UIP or equality reflection.
The implementation must include full dependent eliminators whose later motives can use the results of earlier eliminators, with propositional constructor equations.
The generic published reduction uses an extensional foundation, while the checked UIP-free constructions cover more restricted settings or signatures.
A resolution would determine whether this important form of dependent datatype needs a new primitive in the explicitly chosen intensional foundation.

definitions:
Base theory. \(\mathsf T\) is intensional Martin-Löf type theory with the cumulative predicative hierarchy \(\mathcal U_0:\mathcal U_1:\cdots\), dependent products \(\Pi\), dependent sums \(\Sigma\), the unit type, natural numbers, intensional identity types with reflexivity and the dependent identity eliminator \(J\), indexed W-types, and dependent function extensionality. The ordinary introductions, dependent eliminators and their judgmental beta rules are available; equality reflection and UIP are not rules or axioms. Function extensionality says that pointwise identity of dependent functions yields their identity. There is no additional univalence, cubical composition, quotient, higher inductive or inductive-inductive primitive. An indexed W-type is the well-founded tree family \(W:I\to\mathcal U_i\) for small data \(I\), shapes \(A(i)\), positions \(B(i,a)\) and child index \(s(i,a,b)\), with constructors \(\mathsf{sup}_i(a,f):W(i)\) for \(f:\prod_{b:B(i,a)}W(s(i,a,b))\), and its full dependent tree eliminator. Finite auxiliary universe increases in an encoding must be explicitly supplied and justified within this hierarchy; no resizing or impredicative universe is granted.

Signatures. A signature is a finite telescope of declarations in an external context. Its signature types are generated by a sort-code type \(U\), decoding \(\mathsf{El}(a)\) for a signature term \(a:U\), and dependent products \((x:\mathsf{El}(a))\to B\) and \((x:T)\to B\). In the first product, \(a\) is a sort code and \(B\) is again a signature type. In the second, \(T\) is a type of the external base theory, independent of the sorts being constructed; external types and families may depend on external parameters and are not assumed to have UIP. Terms of the signature language are declared variables, their well-typed applications and substitutions. The external expressions are finite base-theory expressions, with free parameters allowed. There is no signature identity-type former, equality constructor, lambda abstraction over inductive arguments, or function-valued recursive argument. Products bind individual recursive elements; each constructor has finitely many recursive arguments. A declaration ending in \(U\) introduces a sort or a family of sorts; one ending in \(\mathsf{El}(a)\) introduces a constructor. Later declarations may refer to earlier sort and constructor declarations. Universe levels are ordinary natural-number levels; all sorts, external types and motives are assigned levels admitted by the cumulative hierarchy. The construction is a derived-rule schema over all such level instances, with no requirement that its intermediate encoding live in the least available universe.

Algebras and dependent elimination. An algebra interprets each sort as a type or indexed family and each constructor as a term of its declared type. A displayed algebra supplies, over every interpreted sort element, a motive type; this type may also depend on the displayed elements of all earlier indices. For each constructor it supplies a method returning the corresponding motive, given the constructor arguments and displayed arguments for every recursive element. External arguments are passed unchanged. The displayed translation follows the telescope in order: duplicate each inductive argument by its motive inhabitant, substitute both components in later dependent declarations, and interpret a sort code as a family over its interpreted type. A section supplies an eliminator for every sort, into its motive, using the earlier eliminators for displayed indices; for each constructor, applying the eliminator to that constructor must equal its supplied method applied to the arguments and their recursive images. These equations are identity-type inhabitants in \(\mathsf T\), with the transports required by the dependent types. They need not hold by judgmental reduction.

For example, for \(\mathsf{Con}:\mathcal U_i\) and \(\mathsf{Ty}:\mathsf{Con}\to\mathcal U_i\), full motives have types \(P:\mathsf{Con}\to\mathcal U_j\) and \(Q:\prod_{\Gamma:\mathsf{Con}}P(\Gamma)\to\mathsf{Ty}(\Gamma)\to\mathcal U_j\). The required eliminators have types \(e_C:\prod_\Gamma P(\Gamma)\) and \(e_T:\prod_\Gamma\prod_{A:\mathsf{Ty}(\Gamma)}Q(\Gamma,e_C(\Gamma),A)\). Omitting the \(P(\Gamma)\) argument of \(Q\) gives a weaker principle. UIP would assert \(\prod_{X:\mathcal U_i}\prod_{x,y:X}\prod_{p,q:\mathsf{Id}_X(x,y)}\mathsf{Id}(p,q)\); it must not be smuggled in by requiring all external types to be sets.

Effectiveness means one terminating procedure on finite encodings of well-formed signature and base-theory derivations, producing finite terms and typing/equation derivations, uniformly in the open external context. Substitution of external parameters must yield valid instances of the construction. There is no time, space or output-size bound. This is an exact existence-of-construction question, not a numerical approximation problem.
answer_criterion: An accepted answer is a complete Lean proof of the existence of the uniform derived-rule construction just specified, or of its negation. A positive answer must represent the object theory \(\mathsf T\), its signature syntax and permitted derivations, and verify the generated sort/constructor terms, full dependent eliminators, transports and propositional beta proofs for all signatures and universe instances. A suitably formalized semantic argument qualifies if it establishes that exact derived-rule conclusion; a construction in one stronger model alone does not. A negative answer must rule out the stated uniform construction; proving that one proposed encoding uses UIP is insufficient. A model of the stated base theory in which an allowed signature has no required implementation can establish a negative answer if the relevant soundness implication is proved. Lean's native equality lies in its proof-irrelevant proposition sort and cannot stand in for the object theory's possibly higher identity types: represent the latter as syntax or semantic type data, and check that neither UIP nor equality reflection enters the object derivations. This editorial completion does not itself provide a Lean formalization.

source_formulation.text: Can finitary inductive-inductive types, including their full dependent elimination principles, be reduced to inductive types in a foundation without UIP?
source_formulation.caption: Editorial paraphrase of the source question; the card selects the explicitly approved intensional MLTT variant

context_blocks.text: An inductive-inductive declaration defines several sorts together, allowing a later sort to be indexed by an earlier one. Contexts and context-indexed types are a basic example: a context constructor can consume a type over that context, so the two constructions are mutually dependent.

The source gives a generic reduction of finitary IITs to indexed W-types in an extensional setting. Definition 1 includes both UIP and equality reflection; Corollary 58 therefore does not already prove the selected intensional claim. Section 5 treats infinitely branching IITs as a separate extension.

Full dependent elimination retains the result of eliminating earlier indices as arguments to later motives. This recursive dependency is stronger than simultaneous induction with motives independent of those results. The source states the general UIP-free question in Remark 47 and again in its conclusion.

Hugunin proves that one earlier pre-syntax-and-goodness construction, equipped even with its simple eliminator, would imply UIP. The same paper develops one parameterized cubical example. The obstruction is to that encoding, while the positive example uses a different base theory and a weaker elimination specification.
A December 2025 workshop programme lists a talk on reduction without UIP. The inspected programme gives no theorem or linked proof, so its title alone cannot establish a resolution.

A May 2026 cubical Agda artifact implements a particular closed context/type signature and states full dependent motives. It is not a generic signature construction, and its checked snapshot contains four postulates labelled provable. The artifact was read but not typechecked; it does not certify the selected MLTT target.

Scope decision, 16 September 2026: the user chose intensional MLTT with cumulative universes, dependent products and sums, identity and natural-number types, indexed W-types and function extensionality, without UIP or equality reflection, requiring full dependent elimination with propositional beta equations. This explicitly specializes the source programme; a cubical construction or a demand for judgmental equations is a different variant.
